What photo works best?
One clear, close photo of one area: an ear, a paw, the teeth or a patch of skin. Daylight is best. Avoid flash glare.
What happens to my photo?
It is made smaller on your device and used only for that scan. We don’t sell or publish it.
What if it can’t tell?
You’ll be asked for a closer, well-lit photo. Or describe what you can see and we’ll match it to our symptom guide.
Do I need to be online?
Yes, photos are scanned online. Describing what you see works without a connection.

We started Poorly Pet after our own Dachshund, Marble, was diagnosed with IVDD. What we learned helping her became a simple mission: make the right support easy to find for every poorly pet.

In 2024, at just three years old, our much-loved Dachshund Marble was diagnosed with IVDD. We had first noticed her dragging her back legs and losing her balance. Almost overnight we were learning words like “disc extrusion” and “crate rest”.
We couldn’t find the right help, so we kept looking. Late nights reading studies, forums and vet guidance taught us one thing: good products existed, but finding the right ones was far too hard.

We tested products, read everything we could and kept what genuinely helped. With patience and careful monitoring, Marble’s better days started to outnumber her bad ones, and we began sharing what we had learned with other dog owners.
At the end of 2025, Joe and Lily founded Poorly Pet from home in Sandbach, Cheshire: one place for guidance and carefully chosen products for recovery, comfort and everyday wellbeing.

Why Is My Dog Licking Their Paws?

A bit of paw-licking is normal grooming. But if your dog is constantly licking, chewing or nibbling their paws, sometimes to the point of red, sore skin, there’s usually an underlying reason worth tracking down. Here are the common causes and what helps.
In this guide
Common reasons for paw-licking
What to check
How to help
Why Is My Dog Licking Their Paws?, answered
Signs to look for

Allergies are the number-one cause, to pollen, grass, food or things in the environment. Other reasons include irritation, a trapped grass seed, dry or cracked pads, a paw injury, or even boredom and stress when it becomes a habit.
Have a good look (and sniff) at the paws.
Redness or soreness between the toes and on the pads
A brown stain on the fur from constant licking
Cracked or dry pads
Anything stuck between the toes, like a grass seed
A pattern, after walks, certain times of year, or when bored
Soothe the skin and tackle the cause.
Wipe and dry paws after walks, especially in allergy season
Soothing balms for dry or irritated pads
Omega oils to support skin and coat from within
Keep on top of flea and parasite prevention
Address boredom with enrichment if licking is habitual
When to see your vet.
See your vet if the skin is broken, sore, swollen or smelly, or the licking is constant, persistent paw-licking often needs an allergy or infection treating before it will settle.
It’s often a sign of contact allergies to grass or pollen. Wiping the paws after walks and a soothing routine can help.
Can paw-licking be a habit?
Yes, what starts with irritation can become a habit, especially in bored or anxious dogs. Enrichment and addressing the cause both help.
Omega oils support the skin barrier and coat condition, which can reduce dryness and irritation over time.
Itchy Skin and Allergies in Dogs: Causes and Soothing Solutions

Few things are more frustrating than a dog that just won’t stop scratching. Itchy skin is one of the most common reasons dogs visit the vet, and it has many possible causes. Here’s how to work out what’s behind it and soothe your dog’s skin.
Cracked Paw Pads in Dogs: Care and Prevention

Your dog’s paw pads take a daily battering, hot pavements, icy ground, rough terrain and harsh chemicals all take their toll. Dry, cracked pads are sore and can let in infection. A little care keeps them soft, healthy and resilient.
Seasonal Allergies in Dogs: Spotting and Soothing the Itch

Does your dog start scratching every spring or summer? Seasonal allergies, usually to pollen, are extremely common, and they can make life miserable for itchy dogs. While there’s no quick cure, a consistent routine keeps the itch under control through the worst months.
